Everything to get started - claim and bond a horse, read its stats, ride smarter, and how breeding and coats work.
The five horse classes, the breeds inside each, and what every one of them can do.
Every craft in the mod, with a note on when each piece is worth making.

A JSON config at **config/icys-better-horses.json** lets you toggle whole systems without removing the mod. Server admins use it to decide what's available on a world.   
    
With **Cloth Config** installed you can edit the same settings in game instead.

Every key takes **yes** or **no**:   
    
- **stabilizer** - gliding descent.   
- **medkit** - auto-heal on low health.   
- **hitchpost** - tethering blocks.   
- **hooves** - frost-walk, step-up, and fall-damage perks.   
- **horse_exclusivity** - owner-only riding.   
- **multiriding** - two riders on one horse.
Items disabled in the config don't vanish - they switch to **dummy mode** and stay craftable as decorative models only. Nothing fires off in the world, but you can still build a display stable.
Press your **Horse Whistle** key while mounted to open a full profile of the horse you're riding. Pressing it without a horse still whistles your nearby mount.

- **Gender** and **Breed** (with a **(mix)** tag if cross-bred).   
- **Coat** - color plus markings.   
- **Bond** - value out of 100 with a fill bar.   
- **Speed** - blocks per second.   
- **Jump** - block height.   
- **Health** - hit points.

Each bar fills toward the mod's ceiling, not this horse's own range:   
    
- Speed up to **26.25 blk/s**.   
- Jump up to **9.71 blk**.   
- Health up to **50 HP**.   
    
The speed and jump ceilings already include the full-bond bonus, so a strong horse still reads short until it is bonded. Health does not grow with bond.
An owned horse only answers to you. Anyone else who tries to ride it as the main rider is bucked off at once. It will still accept a second rider - but only while you're already in the saddle.

To let one particular player ride on their own, type **/horse trust PlayerName**. It covers every horse you own, now and later, and **/horse untrust** takes it back.   
    
See **Trusted Riders** for what that does and doesn't hand over.

Servers can turn this off in **config/icys-better-horses.json** by setting **horse_exclusivity** to **no** - then any player can ride any owned horse, handy for shared stables. The same file also toggles stabilizers, medkits, hitchposts, hooves, and multi-riding.
Tame a horse fully and it becomes **owned** and starts using Better Horses' systems.

Look at an owned horse and press your **Horse Command Wheel** key to open the radial menu. Pick a wedge to issue it, or click outside to cancel.   
    
- **Follow**: the horse trails after you.   
- **Wander**: it grazes and roams a 32x32 area around where you gave the command.   
- **Stay**: it waits where you left it.   
- **Set Home**: marks the spot as home and switches to Stay.   
- **Return Home**: sends it back to that saved spot.

Press your **Horse Whistle** key to whistle for your horse. Nearby mounts switch to **Follow**; distant ones are pulled closer. While riding, the same key opens the horse's info screen instead.   
    
Bond runs 0 to 100, and every 20 points adds speed and jump strength.   
    
- Stay near your horse for slow passive gain.   
- A **Name Tag** gives +10 bond.   
- A **Golden Apple** gives +2 bond.

Owner-only riding doesn't have to mean nobody else. Type **/horse trust PlayerName** and that player may ride every horse you own.   
    
Trust is stored per player, not per horse, so it also covers every horse you tame later. You never have to run it again for a new mount.

A trusted rider is treated as you are. They may mount your horse, ride behind you, take the reins of a cart, open its gear screen, use its saddlebags and the cart's chest, fit a cart or stabilizer, shear its saddle, hitch it, and give it commands.   
    
The one thing they **cannot** do is disown it. Releasing a horse stays with its owner, so nobody you trust can give your horse away.

**/horse untrust PlayerName** revokes it. If they're in the saddle at that moment, the horse bucks them off on the spot.   
    
**/horse trusted** lists everyone you currently trust.   
    
A trusted rider can ride your horse away, and you can't whistle it out from under them. Only trust people you'd hand a lead to.
Better Horses turns an ordinary mount into a lasting companion, with ownership, bonding, and a stack of riding fixes. This handbook covers all of it.
Tame a horse and it's registered to you right away. From there you can bond with it, equip it, and give it commands.

Press your **Manage Horses** key to open the roster. It lists every horse registered to you, wherever it is - following you, parked at home, or standing in another dimension.   
    
A horse marked **Resting** is in an unloaded chunk. It's safe, and it still answers the whistle.

Pick a horse and it appears in 3D on the right, so you can tell your horses apart!   
    
Three lines sit under the model:   
    
- Its **coordinates**, as X, Y, Z.   
- Its **bond**, out of 100.   
- Whether it has a **home** set.

The coordinates are the fastest way to go fetch a mount that's too far off to whistle, or resting in another dimension.   
    
For a horse loaded nearby, the numbers follow it as it moves. For a resting one, they're the last spot it stood in - which is exactly where you'll find it. They're always given in that horse's own dimension, shown beside its gender in the list.

- **Set Active** - the horse your whistle calls from now on.   
- **Whistle** - calls it to you; it walks if it's close, teleports if it isn't.   
- **Send Home** - packs it off to its saved home.   
- **Disown** - gives it up for good, after a confirmation. Strip its gear first.

Bold patchwork coats are their signature with dramatic **white field** patterns.   
    
Speed: **8-15** blk/s   
Jump: **2-4** blk   
Health: **15-30**

**At bond 0:** A map filled from the saddle covers twice the usual ground.   
    
**At bond 40:** Three times the usual ground.   
    
**At bond 100:** Four times, and structures it rides past get marked on the map. The marking reads the game's own structure list, so modded structures show up too.

An agile, strong Iberian breed with a thick mane, common across open meadows.   
    
Speed: **9-15** blk/s   
Jump: **2-5** blk   
Health: **25-40**

**At bond 0:** The rider takes reduced damage while mounted.   
    
**At bond 40:** That reduction gets stronger.   
    
**At bond 100:** **Second Chance**: a blow that would kill you is taken by the horse instead, and the horse lives through it on one heart. Long cooldown.

Known for its leopard-spot pattern - the only breed whose coat always carries **dots**. Tough and athletic.   
    
Speed: **8-15** blk/s   
Jump: **2-4** blk   
Health: **15-30**

**At bond 0:** Night vision while you ride it in the dark, no torch needed.   
    
**At bond 40:** **Herding**: while you are in the saddle, livestock within **20 blocks** trail after the horse with nothing in your hand, and keep up at a trot or a canter. Pause it per horse from the command wheel.   
    
**At bond 100:** **Auto-feed**: with a chest equipped it hands animals within **12 blocks** the right breeding food from its own storage.

Compact and hardy, bred for tough country. A strong choice for desert crossings and badlands runs.   
    
Speed: **11-15** blk/s   
Jump: **3-5.5** blk   
Health: **15-20**

**At bond 0:** Speed builds while you keep moving, up to +10%% after twenty seconds. Stopping bleeds it away at 2%% a second.   
    
**At bond 40:** The ceiling doubles to +20%%.   
    
**At bond 100:** You reach the ceiling in twelve seconds, and a two second grace means a brief pause no longer wipes the climb.

Belgium's draft breed, and pound for pound the strongest horse here. Broader through the barrel than a Percheron and heavily feathered on all four legs, it pulls where the others carry.   
    
Speed: **7-10** blk/s   
Jump: **1-3** blk   
Health: **35-50**

**At bond 0:** Six rows of storage, two above any other draft and the biggest chest in the mod.   
    
**At bond 40:** Seats three riders, as long as it is not carrying a chest.   
    
**At bond 100:** **Brick Break**: at a full gallop it punches a **three-wide, three-tall** hole through weak blocks. It costs the horse health and needs half a minute to recover.

Scotland's draft giant, and the showiest of the four. It is a carriage and parade horse before it is a ploughing one.   
    
Speed: **7-10** blk/s   
Jump: **1-3** blk   
Health: **35-50**

**At bond 0:** Equipped barding grants **25%% more armour**. Charge and kick damage read armour too, giving a modest damage bonus.   
    
**At bond 40:** Wearing barding grants the rider Resistance.   
    
**At bond 100:** **Deflect**: arrows and other projectiles are stopped before they land.

The all-black horse of the Dutch lowlands - tall and powerful, always show-ready.   
    
Speed: **9-15** blk/s   
Jump: **2-5** blk   
Health: **25-40**

**At bond 0:** Neutral mobs lose interest in you, and anything already angry drops the grudge.   
    
**At bond 40:** The same calm extends to hostile mobs.   
    
**At bond 100:** **Dressage**: rear the horse and every hostile in front is thrown back and loses its target.

A small Tyrolean mountain breed with a chestnut body and flaxen mane. Sure-footed on slopes.   
    
Speed: **8-13** blk/s   
Jump: **2-4** blk   
Health: **25-40**

**At bond 0:** Four rows of storage, a row above what a pony has any right to.   
    
**At bond 40:** Pulls a cart with no speed penalty, normally a draft horse's job.   
    
**At bond 100:** Six rows, level with the Belgian, plus **Hearthlight**: after dark it glows and lights the ground it walks over.

A short, shaggy, cold-hardy pony from Iceland, known for an unusually smooth extra gait.   
    
Speed: **8-13** blk/s   
Jump: **2-4** blk   
Health: **25-40**

**At bond 0:** Soul sand, cobwebs, berries and honey do not slow it down.   
    
**At bond 40:** **Winter Coat**: neither horse nor rider freezes, whatever the weather.   
    
**At bond 100:** **Clear Head**: nothing bad sticks to **either of you**. Poison, wither and hunger are refused outright, on the pony whether you are riding it or not, and on you while you are on its back.

A compact, hardworking American breed - versatile enough for the trail or the field.   
    
Speed: **8-15** blk/s   
Jump: **2-4** blk   
Health: **15-30**

**At bond 0:** Bonds **half again as fast** as any other horse. Time near you, golden apples and the first name tag all count for more.   
    
**At bond 40:** That climbs to **double**.   
    
**At bond 100:** **Adaptable**: a slice of every other class at once, including a fourth storage row and a higher step.

A free-roaming North American horse - tough, weatherproof, and rarely the same coat twice.   
    
Speed: **9-15** blk/s   
Jump: **2-5** blk   
Health: **25-40**

**At bond 0:** Hostiles nearby are outlined for a few seconds and the horse snorts a warning. It also heals itself, without food - **a heart every 15 seconds**.   
    
**At bond 40:** Its own healing climbs to **a heart every 8 seconds**, and it begins healing **you** as well - **a heart every 10 seconds** while you are in the saddle.   
    
**At bond 100:** Rider healing doubles to **a heart every 5 seconds**.

A French draft breed - heavy and muscular, but graceful for its size.   
    
Speed: **7-10** blk/s   
Jump: **1-3** blk   
Health: **35-50**

**At bond 0:** Soul sand, cobwebs, sweet berries and honey do not slow it down.   
    
**At bond 40:** **Momentum**: the longer it runs in a straight line the harder its charge lands, up to half again at full wind.   
    
**At bond 100:** **Chain Charge**: a charge that kills leaves no cooldown, so it can run straight through a group.

Stocky and broad-chested, very fast over short distances. A reliable all-purpose ranch horse.   
    
Speed: **11-15** blk/s   
Jump: **3-5.5** blk   
Health: **15-20**

**At bond 0:** Stand still for a second, then move off, and you get +30%% for 5 seconds. Ten second cooldown.   
    
**At bond 40:** The burst climbs to +45%%.   
    
**At bond 100:** Cooldown drops to 8 seconds.

England's largest draft horse - taller than a Clydesdale and just as patient. Heavy feathering on all four legs is the breed's signature.   
    
Speed: **7-10** blk/s   
Jump: **1-3** blk   
Health: **35-50**

**At bond 0:** Anything that has locked onto you but has not swung yet gets snorted and stamped at, and usually thinks better of it. Once it has hit you, it is too late.   
    
**At bond 40:** The radius widens.   
    
**At bond 100:** **Brick Break**, the same as the Belgian’s: a galloping Shire punches a **three-wide, three-tall** hole through weak blocks.

The classic racing horse - tall, lean, and built for speed. An easy first pick for long rides.   
    
Speed: **11-15** blk/s   
Jump: **3-5.5** blk   
Health: **15-20**

**At bond 0:** +35%% speed for 3 seconds whenever you gallop on level ground, then 5 seconds before it can fire again. There is no wind-up.   
    
**At bond 40:** The burst climbs to +50%%.   
    
**At bond 100:** The burst lasts 5 seconds instead of 3, so you spend about half your time boosted.
The heavy tier. Slowest legs, most hearts, worst jump, and the only horses that will carry a chest and two riders at the same time.

Four rows of storage as standard.   
A chest **and** two riders, which no other class allows.   
Pulls a loaded cart at full speed, where every other class drags at -30%%.   
Heavy knockback resistance.   
Charge damage 1.25x, and the hardest knockback in the game at 2x.   
Spooks at half the usual rate.
Small, stubborn and much harder to kill than they look. Ponies go places the big breeds physically cannot.

Steps **two full blocks** without jumping, where every other horse steps one.   
No fall damage under 15 blocks.   
Walks on powder snow with no hoof gear.   
Heals slowly on its own, without food.   
Charge and kick damage 0.75x, and the light knockback of a race horse.   
Standard spook chance.

The fastest legs in the stable, sitting on a single row of hearts. Race horses jump higher than anything else here and hit softest of all in a charge.   
    
All three get their speed a different way, so the ground you ride decides which one actually wins.

Fastest speed and highest jump of any class.   
Lowest health in the game.   
Charge and kick damage 0.6x, the weakest.   
Standard spook chance.

Every horse belongs to one of five classes. The class sets the range its speed, health and jump are rolled from, and hands out a set of perks shared by every breed in it.   
    
The breed on top of that decides your one unique ability, and that ability grows twice: once at **bond 40**, again at **bond 100**.
The horses you take somewhere dangerous. Nearly the toughest in the game, and the only ones that will not panic on you.

**Never spook**, at any bond level.   
Never rear when struck, so you keep your seat and your heading.   
Medkits last twice as long.   
Charge and kick damage 1.5x, the highest.

Stock horses, built for ground you have already worked. Give them a road and they pick up speed on it.   
    
Health and pace sit close to an ordinary horse. What you are buying is everything around the riding.

+10%% speed on roads, rising to +20%% at bond 40 and +50%% at bond 100.   
Roads means paths, gravel, cobble, brick and anything tagged `horse_road`.   
Standard damage and spook chance.
A small copper-and-gold capsule. It does little alone, but the stabilizer can't be built without it.
Think of the canister as the working end of the stabilizer. Craft it first, then build the full rig when you're ready to protect a horse from falls.
A **Lead** and any block in the **Fences** tag. Simple to build, very useful.
Place a hitchpost near a ridden horse, or near another owned horse, to tether it. It only works with your own horses; breaking it releases the tether.
Two **Wheels**, a row of planks for the bed, and two slabs on top. Make the wheels first.

Slot the cart into the **Upgraded Saddle** and it appears behind your horse, rolling along as you ride. It shares the stabilizer's slot, so a horse carries one or the other - not both.   
    
Quickest way to fit one: right-click the horse while holding the cart. It goes straight on, as long as the horse wears an Upgraded Saddle and that slot is empty.

Right-click the ground with the cart to stand one up on its own, shafts down, no horse needed. A parked cart is decoration, but a **Chest** works on it exactly as it does on a hitched one.   
    
Hit it a few times to pick it back up, like a boat. Break one with a chest fitted and the chest and everything in it come down with it.

A small cart seats four. Two share the driver's bench up front - whoever takes it first drives the horse - and two more ride in the bed behind. The large cart carries **six**, four of them in the bed.   
    
Animals that wander into the bed climb aboard on their own, and once you're driving, one can ride shotgun in the free seat beside you. The cart takes anything a **boat** would.   
    
**Sneak** and right-click an animal to set it down, or the cart itself to unload the lot.

Right-click the cart with a **Chest** in hand to mount it in the bed. **Sneak** and right-click the cart to open it: a full **double chest** on the small one, and **ninety** slots on the large.   
    
A chest fills a small bed, so that cart carries no back-seat passengers - the driver's bench still seats two. The large cart has room to spare and keeps two of its four bed seats.

Right-click the small cart with any **hoe** and a plough drops down behind the bed. Drive over grass, dirt or coarse dirt and it turns a **three-wide** strip into farmland as you go.   
    
The hoe wears down a point for every block it turns, and when it finally breaks the plough comes off with it, so bring a good one - **enchantments still count**.   
    
**Shears** take the plough back off. Fit a chest as well and the shears take the plough first, the chest second.   
    
Only the small cart takes a plough. The big wagon has no room for one.

**Shears** take the chest back off and drop it beside the horse. But empty it first, a loaded chest refuses to come off.   
    
Things come off in the order they went on, and the slot flashes **red** if you try to skip a step: shear the chest off before unhitching the cart, and unhitch the cart before taking the saddle off.
A few copper ingots and a leather strap give your mount a steadier step in rough country.
Hooves let a horse walk on powder snow instead of falling through, and soften fall damage - good everyday tack for mountains and cold biomes.
Hooves take **Frost Walker** at an **Anvil** from an enchanted book. A horse running over water then leaves a trail of **frosted ice**, like a player wearing frost-walker boots.
The freeze radius depends on the **Frost Walker enchantment level**. The trail is sampled along the horse's movement so fast horses do not outrun it. Lava still isn't safe.
Emergency tack. Wrap wool, healing supplies, and a regeneration potion together before heading somewhere dangerous.

If a hit would drop your horse below half health, the medkit is used up and grants **Regeneration**, **Instant Health**, **Resistance**, and **Fire Resistance** - often the difference between a close call and a dead horse.
Bind your canisters into the full stabilizer and mount it on the upgraded saddle.

Built for ravines and cliffs. During big falls it deploys, slows the descent, and can cancel fall damage entirely.   
    
Right-click the horse holding the stabilizer to fit it, as long as it wears an Upgraded Saddle and that slot is empty. Horses only - mules, donkeys and the undead sort can't wear one.(I'm too lazy to make seperate models)
Every craft in the tack room, gathered here for a quick reference.
Any **Better Horses** item plus a **Book** makes a fresh handbook - easy to replace or hand to another player.
Keep one in your travel chest and one at home. It's cheap to remake whenever you need it.
The core of the tack room. A vanilla **Saddle**, some copper, and a few diamonds turn your horse into a gear hauler.
Once equipped, the **Upgraded Saddle** opens five gear slots: **Chest**, **Hooves**, **Medkit**, **Stabilizer**, and **Hitchpost**. Most of the mod's equipment starts here.
Put a plain **Chest** in the chest slot for 27 storage slots on the horse screen. Empty it before removing it, or the contents drop.

Use an **Ender Chest** instead and those 27 slots become your **Ender Inventory**, shared with every ender chest you own. Swapping back to a normal chest or pulling the ender chest keeps its contents.

Hold the **Upgraded Saddle** and look at any horse to show a **Horse Stats** panel above your hotbar:   
    
- **Gender**   
- **Breed**   
- **Speed** - blocks per second   
- **Jump** - block height   
    
Handy for checking wild stock before taming.
Sticks for the spokes, planks for the rim and hub - any wood works. You'll need two to build a cart.
A wheel alone doesn't do much. Pair two with planks and slabs to build a **Horse Cart**.

Two horses of the same gender won't mate. Feed a **Golden Apple** to a horse whose partner matches its gender and you'll see "These horses are the same gender and can't breed." The apple is still used and love mode resets.

When a foal is born:   
    
- **Gender** is a coin flip.   
- **Breed** comes from one parent at 50/50. Matching parents pass it cleanly; different breeds give the foal a **(mix)** tag.   
- Cross-species pairs (horse + donkey) give the matching species placeholder.

Health, speed, and jump are **max(parent1, parent2) + delta**, where delta is a roll from **-0.5** to **+1.0**. Foals can beat both parents, but the ceiling is the vanilla base - no runaway superhorses.

The foal's coat always comes from the palette its inherited breed allows. Two **Quarter** horses always give a Quarter-pattern coat; a mixed pair can surprise you with either side's palette.   
    
Which coat it gets is a coin flip. **Half** the time the foal wears one of its parents' coats. The other half it comes out in a coat **neither parent wears**, so two black Shires will often throw a bay or a roan.

Beyond **Bond**, every horse now carries four pieces of identity:   
    
- **Gender** - male or female. Even donkeys and mules have one.   
- **Breed** - one of fifteen real breeds for plain horses; a species label for donkeys, mules, and skeleton or zombie horses.   
- **Mixed-Breed** - a **(mix)** tag when a foal inherits two breeds.   
- **Coat** - color and markings, tied to the breed.

Press your **Horse Whistle** key while mounted to open the **Horse Info Screen** - gender, breed, coat, and stat bars are all there. Holding the **Upgraded Saddle** and looking at a horse also shows its gender and breed under its name.
A ridden horse should feel responsive. Better Horses fixes a list of small frictions vanilla horses used to have.

- Step height is raised by a tenth, so a galloping horse doesn't trip over slabs, paths, or full blocks.   
- Mounted block-breaking now matches on-foot speed for most blocks.   
- Whatever penalty is left after that is cut to a fifth.

Mounting no longer snaps your camera to the horse's facing - the **horse turns to match you** instead. Standing still, you get up to **90 degrees** of free look before the horse follows, so you can scan the horizon without dismounting.
Using a **Saddle** (vanilla or upgraded) on a horse in **Creative Mode** tames it instantly - no waiting on hearts. Useful when testing builds.

Better Horses smooths out mounted travel.   
    
- Two players can share one horse for co-op trips.   
- The first rider keeps the reins.   
- The second gets a back seat.
Double-tap **W** while riding to enable auto-ride: the horse keeps moving forward and you just steer. Tap a movement key again to take back full control.

Horses handle bad terrain better now.   
    
- They float instead of sinking in water.   
- They move faster crossing water.   
- Leaf blocks lose collision while you ride, so forests feel like a path.

Press your **Horse Walk Cycle** key while riding to shift up a gait. It runs **Walk**, **Trot**, **Canter**, **Gallop**, then back to a halt, and whichever you land on prints over your hotbar.   
    
Once a gait is set the horse holds it on its own. You steer, and never touch **W**.

- **Walk** - about **2** blk/s.   
- **Trot** - about **4.4** blk/s.   
- **Canter** - about **6.8** blk/s.   
- **Gallop** - the horse's own top speed, whatever that is.   
    
The first three are set paces, so a plough horse and a racer walk side by side at the same speed. Only the gallop shows what a fast horse is really worth, and a horse slower than the pace you asked for just gives you everything it has.

Hold **W** or **S** and the gait steps aside for as long as you hold it, then picks straight back up where it was. One more press past **Gallop** brings the horse down to a halt.   
    
Double-tapping **W** for cruise clears the gait outright, and so does stepping off the horse or climbing onto another one.

A horse at a full **gallop** in a straight line is a weapon. Whatever you steer into takes the hit, with no swing of your own.   
    
The charge needs about **a second** of straight movement to arm itself and keeps building for **three**. Turning sharply or stopping resets the wind-up. Slower straight movement and jumps keep it building.   
    
It only fires on the ground with a rider aboard, and only at a true gallop - free riding, or the **Gallop** gait.

A meter sits beside your hotbar while you gallop, filling as the charge winds up. A full one means the next thing you touch gets all of it, and after a hit it refills over about **five seconds**. A **Percheron** at bond 100 skips that wait whenever its charge kills, so it can run straight through a group.

The base hit is **7** damage, scaled by the class: **War** 1.5x, **Draft** 1.25x, **Western** 1x, **Pony** 0.75x, **Race** 0.6x.   
    
- **Horse armor** adds up to **3** on top. A **Clydesdale** wears it better and gets up to **5**.   
- Speed and wind-up scale the whole thing, close to double it on a long straight run.   
- Nothing lands harder than **30**.   
    
Draft horses throw a target furthest, war horses next. The light classes barely shift it.

A fight your horse picks is not always one it can win. Your **Horse Whistle** key breaks off every horse you own that is fighting or already bolting.   
    
They do not trot back to you. Calling them off sends them running for about **three seconds**, which is the point: it pulls a horse out from under something far too big for it. Whistle again once they have put some ground between themselves and the fight.

The charge leaves out everything you would rather keep:   
    
- You, and anyone riding with you.   
- Players you **trust**.   
- Other horses you own.   
- Anything allied to you or to the horse.   
    
The rest of the field in front of the horse is fair game.

Come at a horse from behind and it kicks, using the same class multiplier as the charge. Owned or wild, saddled or loose, they all do it.   
    
Its owner, anyone that owner trusts, and whoever is in the saddle never take one. After it kicks, a horse that is not already defending someone bolts for about three seconds.

When something hurts you, every horse you own within **16 blocks** knows about it.   
    
A loose horse at **bond 40** or better goes for your attacker, chasing it down and running it over. It breaks off if it drops under a third of its health, or if the fight drags more than **32 blocks** from where it started. A horse told to **Stay** stays.

The horse under you reacts the other way: it may panic and throw you off.   
    
The odds drop as it comes to trust you - **10%%** at first, **7%%** at bond 40, **5%%** at bond 100. **Draft** horses spook half as often, and a **War** horse never does. It will not dump you in midair or over a long drop.   
    
Charge, kick and defence are one switch: set **horse_combat** to **no** in the config to turn the lot off.

Fit a cart to a **draft** horse and you get the big one, a covered wagon on four wheels. Every other class pulls the small two-wheeled cart.   
    
Look at the horse or the cart and press your **Swap Cart Size** key to change your mind, either way, at any time. A parked cart takes it too.   
    
Only draft horses may go large. A cart also refuses to change if its passengers or its load would not fit the new bed, or if a parked one has no room to grow.

Press your **Rear Horse** key to put a horse up on its hind legs. It works on the horse you are riding, or on one you are looking at within **12 blocks**.   
    
It has to be a horse you may handle - yours, or one whose owner trusts you - and it ignores you while somebody else holds the reins.   
    
Purely for show. A horse also rears when something strikes it, which costs you a moment's steering, though a **War** horse never does.

Better Horses brings its own branch of advancements. Tame your first horse and the whole tree opens up in the advancements screen.   
    
None of it is required. It is a checklist for a long life in the saddle.

- **Hold Your Horses** - tame a horse.   
- **Stable Reading** - get hold of this book.   
- **All Tacked Up** - craft the Upgraded Saddle.   
- **Home Is Where the Hay Is** - set a horse's home.   
- **Hell on Hooves** - take a horse to the Nether.   
- **Foal Play** - breed two horses.   
- **Best of Both Worlds** - raise a mixed-breed foal.

- **Ride or Die** - reach 100 bond.   
- **Built Different** - ride at 25 blk/s.   
- **Second Chance** - let an Andalusian take a killing blow for you.   
- **Pegasus, Sort Of** - survive a 30 block drop on a stabilizer.   
- **Pocket Dimension, Four Legs** - fit an ender chest.   
- **Stable Genius** - own ten horses at once.   
- **Gotta Tame 'Em All** - own all fifteen breeds.
